title: Scenario Practice: Structuring and Tipping-Off
summary: Make the call in two realistic counter situations, then check the steps and the thresholds. Learn by choosing, and see what each choice leads to.

lessons.title: What to watch for
lessons.body:
## Two things that catch people out

**Structuring** means splitting a transaction into smaller ones to stay under a reporting or identification threshold. **Tipping off** means letting a customer know that a suspicious transaction report has been or may be made. Both can be offences.

In the next lesson you face a situation at the counter and choose what to do. Choices have consequences, so read each step carefully.

*Training summary. Always follow the CBUAE Rulebook and your own policy manual.*

lessons.title: At the counter: a large cash exchange
lessons.body: You are on the counter. Choose what you would do. You can try again, and you finish this lesson by reaching a good outcome.

questions.prompt: A customer offers to split a large amount into smaller transactions "to keep it simple". What is this called?
questions.explanation: Splitting to avoid a threshold is structuring.

questions.prompt: You may warn a customer that a suspicious transaction report is being filed.
questions.explanation: That is tipping off, which is an offence.
